header: Nine years of changeovers, told by the people who sat through them
lead: None of these houses had lost patience with their old system. They had simply outgrown the point where anyone could remember what was on which shelf.

quotes.quote_text: The changeover weekend was the part I dreaded. We opened on the Monday, sold from the counter all day, and I never once had to explain to a customer why the screen said something different from the shelf.
quotes.author: Katrin Weissgruber

quotes.quote_text: What sold it to me was being able to keep our own article numbers. Nobody here was going to learn a new number for a fitting we have sold under the same one since 1998.
quotes.author: Doris Ebner

quotes.quote_text: The first week I checked every reorder suggestion by hand. By the third I was checking the ones it flagged, and by the second month I was only looking at the exceptions.
quotes.author: Ines Kofler

quotes.quote_text: We make to order, so a stock system that only understands boxes on shelves is useless to us. This one lets a half-finished job hold its own material and gives it back if the job is cancelled.
quotes.author: Stefan Aigner

quotes.quote_text: I asked for an export of everything on day one, before I signed anything, and I got it in a format I could open. That answered a question I did not have to ask again.
quotes.author: Hannes Wurzer

quotes.quote_text: Our seasonal peak is eleven weeks long and pays for the year. Going into it with the reorder list working was the first calm autumn I have had here.
quotes.author: Gerald Auracher
